History and Physical (Detailed)

Consult Summary:
65-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and hypertension presents with 5 days of a dry cough and profuse nasal discharge, likely viral upper/lower respiratory tract infection; advised symptomatic care, temperature monitoring, and safety-netting for possible bacterial super-infection.

History:
• Presenting complaint – Dry cough every 20–30 min and continuous nasal “streaming” for 5 days.  
• Timeline – Onset ≈5 days ago; symptoms persistent, not clearly improving.  
• Character – Cough is dry; no sputum, no hemoptysis. Nasal discharge described as green, no epistaxis.  
• Associated symptoms – Subjective fever with alternating chills; myalgias. Initial brief episode of diarrhoea at onset; now resolved. No sore throat, ear pain, headache, chest pain, dyspnoea, wheeze, pleuritic pain, vomiting, current diarrhoea, urinary change, rash, or visual change. Appetite and fluid intake maintained.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors – Lemsip (paracetamol-containing) provides temporary throat relief.  
• Review of systems – as above; remaining systems not discussed.  

Past Medical History:
• Type 2 diabetes mellitus – most recent blood test “normal” (≈3 wks ago); no home glucose monitoring.  
• Hypertension – blood-pressure control status unknown; last check “a while ago.”  
• Denies chronic lung disease; no history of recurrent chest infections.

Medications:
• Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Lisinopril 200 mg (patient-reported dose; high for usual range).  
• Lemsip (paracetamol-containing cold remedy) 2–3 doses/day.  

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.  
• Seasonal hay fever (non-drug).

Social History:
• Lives with partner and a dog.  
• Occupation: Office manager.  
• Alcohol: Occasional (“odd sherry”).  
• Smoking: Not documented.  
• Illicit substances: Not documented.

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
• Vitals: Not recorded.  
• General/Respiratory/ENT/Chest: No physical examination performed or documented.

Investigations:
• None performed during consult.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Probable viral upper/lower respiratory tract infection (cough, rhinorrhoea, subjective fever).  
  • Advise purchase of thermometer; check temperature regularly.  
  • Continue symptomatic treatment with Lemsip; avoid additional paracetamol-containing products.  
  • Encourage hydration and rest.  
  • Small amount of cough syrup acceptable at night only if sleep-deprived; avoid in daytime to aid pulmonary clearance.  
  • Red-flag advice: seek review/ER if temperature ≥37.5–38 °C persists, spikes recur, cough worsens, purulent sputum develops, hemoptysis, dyspnoea, chest pain, or nasal bleeding.  
  • Possible need for antibiotics if features of bacterial infection emerge, especially given diabetes.

Issue 2: Chronic conditions (type 2 diabetes, hypertension).  
  • Patient reminded to attend routine diabetes and blood-pressure follow-ups with GP.  
  • Consider home blood sugar monitoring equipment (patient currently without).  
  • Review lisinopril dose accuracy at next primary-care visit.

General Plan items:
  • Pharmacy purchase of digital thermometer.  
  • Safety-netting instructions emphasised.  
  • No immediate need for antibiotics; watchful waiting advised.  
  • Follow-up: re-contact service if red flags develop or no improvement after 1–2 weeks.

Quality checks:
• Missing but expected: objective vitals, chest/ENT physical exam, smoking status, detailed medication doses, exact diabetes type confirmation, latest HbA1c, allergy clarification beyond “none.”  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear overall; minor inaudible phrases, one questionable lisinopril dose (200 mg) – flagged above.
